verdicts.title: initiateClose() has no access control: anyone can force-close any channel and strand unsettled vouchers

a.reden: Different function and root cause; not the authorized signer zero address issue.

b.reden: The candidate finding describes an access control flaw in initiateClose(), while the known finding addresses a different vulnerability involving zero address signature recovery.

a.reden: The candidate describes a missing deadline validation, which is unrelated to the authorizedSigner zero address validation in H-03

b.reden: The candidate finding about missing deadline validation is unrelated to the known finding about zero address signer validation.

verdicts.title: authorizedSigner may be address(0), letting any invalid signature authorize settle()/close()

a.reden: Describes the same zero‑address authorizedSigner bypass leading to invalid signatures being accepted

b.reden: Both findings describe the same vulnerability where a zero authorizedSigner combined with ecrecover returning zero allows settlement with any invalid signature.

verdicts.title: A voucher whose cumulativeAmount exceeds the deposit cannot be partially settled, which can strand earned funds

a.reden: The candidate describes a different bug (cumulative voucher exceeding deposit) unrelated to the authorized signer zero address issue.

b.reden: The candidate describes a different vulnerability (partial settlement failure due to over-deposit voucher) not related to the known finding (authorized signer bypass).

verdicts.title: Settle vs finalize race at the grace period boundary

a.reden: The candidate describes a race condition, not the zero address signer bypass described in H-03.

b.reden: The candidate describes a race condition in settle/finalize, while the only known finding is about signature validation bypass.

verdicts.title: Any ERC20 accepted, with deposits credited at nominal amount (fee-on-transfer/rebasing insolvency)

a.reden: The candidate describes a fee-on-transfer token deposit accounting issue, which is unrelated to the zero address signer validation bypass in H-03.

b.reden: The candidate describes a fee-on-transfer token vulnerability, while the known finding is about zero address signature validation.

verdicts.title: ecrecover-only signatures: contract-wallet or P256/passkey payers and signers cannot sign vouchers or close

a.reden: The candidate describes a missing ERC-1271 support for contract wallets, which is a different root cause than the zero-address authorizedSigner issue in H-03.

b.reden: The candidate describes a missing support for contract wallets and alternative signature schemes, which is a different root cause and impact than the known finding about zero address signature bypass.

verdicts.title: close() omits expiry/nonce checks and uses a payer signature not bound to chain, contract or nonce

a.reden: The candidate describes missing expiry/nonce checks and an unbound signature in close(), which is a different root cause than the zero-address authorizedSigner bypass in H-03.

b.reden: The candidate describes missing expiry/nonce checks and missing chain/contract binding in the close function, which is a different issue from the known finding about zero address signature recovery.
